newsitem.title: CANADA: Bass brothers gain seat on MacMillan board.
newsitem.headline: Bass brothers gain seat on MacMillan board.

text.p: MacMillan Bloedel Ltd said on Wednesday that Thomas Taylor would join the forestry company's board as a representative of the Bass family and the Ontario Teachers Plan Board.

Last month, Taylor and Co, which invests for the secretive billionaire Bass brothers of Texas, and the Ontario pension fund said they jointly acquired 9.5 percent of MacMillan. That made them the beleaguered company's biggest shareholder.
Thomas Taylor has voting control over the stake, MacMillan Chairman Richard Haskayne told the annual meeting.

Shareholders elected directors at the meeting but the slate did not include Taylor. Haskayne said that was because the annual meeting documents were prepared before the Texas investors and Ontario pension fund bought their stake.
He said the board would appoint Taylor at a directors' meeting on Wednesday afternoon and his election would be confirmed by a vote at next year's shareholder meeting.
Taylor attended the annual meeting, but MacMillan Chief Executive Robert Findlay told reporters that Taylor did not want to speak to the media. The Bass brothers are known for keeping a low profile.
Haskayne said Taylor was invited on the board because his group's interests were "consistent" with the company's.
"We're very comfortable (with the arrangement). We're not frightened," Haskayne said, calling Taylor a "very bright guy."
Asked if Taylor's group supported MacMillan management and the company's direction, Haskayne said, "They've obviously got confidence in us for the long term."
MacMillan has been beset by speculation that it is ripe for a restructuring and has faced complaints from shareholders over its performance.
Analysts have speculated that the entrance of the Bass could hasten a shake-up. Some believe that might include the sale of assets such as the paper division or the spin-off of private timberlands.
Findlay said on Wednesday there were no plans for such moves.
